newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czechs mull plan on transfer of closed-end funds. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Czechs mull plan on transfer of closed-end funds. [CORRECTED 16:55 GMT]

text.p: The Czech finance ministry will present a proposal on how to allow investment funds to transform from closed-end to open-end funds by the end of January, Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus said on Thursday.

"The finance ministry will present to ministers by the 31st of January a proposal the procedure on how to change investment funds from closed into open," Klaus told reporters after meeting finance ministry officials.
He said the procedure might be contained in an amendment to the law on investment funds.

Czech funds which were mostly set up as closed-end funds amid the government's massive voucher-privatisation programmes earlier in the decade, have said they would like to transform in order to expand their shareholder base and avoid the stricter regulation of closed-end funds.

Some of fund managers which have said they would seek to transform their closed-end funds include such major Czech firms as Harvard Capital & Consulting and SIS. (Corrects names of firms which have said they would like to transform funds into open-ended funds)

Many funds avoided new fund regulations passed in the middle of 1996 by transforming into industrial holding companies. The moves brought heavy criticism especially from minority shareholders and foreign investors.
Under the new rules, funds must buy out dissenting shareholders at the full net asset value per share if the fund transforms its status.
